title: Care in the measure each needs
meaning: Your care can feel fair and warm when the amount of help reflects what the two of you actually need.
text: Caring for each other can mean noticing the appropriate measure. Justice in the physical position of Anahata suggests attending to actual requests and sharing participation in a way that is fair to both. The Lovers in energy support freely choosing closeness, responding to someone dear rather than to an abstract duty. Temperance in emotions brings gentle accord: care feels calm when different needs can be combined. Balance need not look like identical help at every moment of the day.

For example, you both have a busy evening, but one person particularly needs to finish an important task. The other can handle small practical matters and receive uninterrupted time later. **Fair care considers the need as well as the number of actions.** You feel participation when the reason for today's arrangement is visible. That understanding brings calm: a difference between you makes neither person's needs less worthy and does not turn support into a permanent debt.

The difficulty begins if peaceful agreement is taken to mean that no new requests exist. You preserve an earlier balance although circumstances have changed, and a previous concession becomes permanent. Protecting fairness then starts to mean counting separate actions. Hearing the need again helps care change its measure while preserving respect for both the person asking and the person offering help.
